query: The Upper Floor {A ladder at the back of Grimsby's climbs through a hatch to an upper floor nobody mentions. "The remainders," says Mr Grimsby vaguely. "Mind the third rung. And the fourth."|The ladder to the upper floor. Someone has tied a ribbon round the third rung, as a warning or a memorial.|The upper floor. You know its geography now: poetry slumps against history, and history has given up.} {Dust swirls in the light from the hatch.|Somewhere up there, something slides and thumps.|{season == "summer": It's stifling under the roof.|Rain drums on the roof right above your head.}} Climb up and rummage {You find a first edition priced at a coin, with a pressed love letter inside. Mr Grimsby buys the book back at twice the price without noticing; the letter you keep.|You dig out a box of old exam papers from the castle, decades old. Mr Grimsby gives them to you for nothing and then pays you to take the box away.|You find a book of spells nobody casts any more, wedged under a shelf to stop it falling. Mr Grimsby gives you a crown for straightening the shelf.} {The third rung breaks, as advertised. You land in a heap of atlases and see stars, and some constellations.|A shelf leans on you, gently, and then less gently. You climb down under a small avalanche of poetry.|The fourth rung, this time. Mr Grimsby looks up from his counter, says "Ah," and goes back to his reading.} Browse the window display {The window display is arranged by colour, not subject. You find three books you didn't know you wanted, and want none of them enough to buy.|You browse the window, where the books have faded through thirty summers. It's a lovely, useless hour.|You browse the window and watch the village go by through the gaps between the spines.}

results.title: Out of Print
results.excerpt:
Out of Print
You need a book for an essay: the one every reading list cites and nobody has seen in thirty years. The library's copy went missing before you arrived. Grimsby, asked, gives you a book about lighthouses instead and says it's the next best thing. He may even be right.
